```{r}
#Packages:
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
#library(rnaturalearth)
#library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(patchwork)
options(useFancyQuotes = FALSE)   # plain quotes in messages (avoids garbled characters on Windows)
```
## 1. Import data
```{r}
#Creating a fuction to read in data
#The data files are in ASCII text, tab delimited
read_tab <- function(file) {
  read.delim(file.path("Data", file), sep = "\t", header = TRUE,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE,
             na.strings = "NA", strip.white = TRUE)
}
#Using the function to import data
macro_orig <- read_tab("Macroplot_data.txt")
macro      <- read_tab("Macroplot_data_Rev.txt")
micro      <- read_tab("Microplot_data.txt")
sites      <- read_tab("Site_variables.txt")
splist     <- read_tab("Species_list.txt")
```

## 2. Check the imported data
Exploring the data frames. Expected values come from the metadata

### 2.1 Macroplot data
```{r}
# structural overview
glimpse(macro_orig)
```
```{r}
glimpse(macro)
```
Individual botanical identifications and girth data for 61965 individuals of 400 tree and liana species (including one unidentified category) with gbh ≥ 10 cm in 96 1-ha macroplots.

Checking how macro tables differ
```{r}
identical(names(macro_orig), names(macro)) #are columns the same?
all.equal(macro_orig, macro)               #short summary of differences
```
Result shows that both files have the same number of rows in the same order but 91 trees have a different species code.
Looking into which SpCode was changed.
```{r}
changed <- which(macro_orig$SpCode != macro$SpCode) #which SpCode code from tables doesnt match

#change results to df
sp_changes <- data.frame(
  PlotID   = macro$PlotID[changed],
  SpCode_orig = macro_orig$SpCode[changed],
  SpCode_rev  = macro$SpCode[changed]
)

#how many trees per "old -> new" pair, and in how many plots
sp_changes %>%
  count(SpCode_orig, SpCode_rev, name = "n_trees") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_trees)) #sort to look at the biggest change

sp_changes %>%
  group_by(SpCode_orig, SpCode_rev) %>%
  summarise(n_trees = n(), n_plots = n_distinct(PlotID),
            plots = paste(unique(PlotID), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#Are the new codes in the species list?
setdiff(unique(sp_changes$SpCode_rev), splist$SpCode)
```
Every corrected species code exists in Species_list.txt, so the revised file is consistent with the species list. 

```{r}
#Were the OLD codes perhaps not in the species list? (would explain the correction)
setdiff(unique(sp_changes$SpCode_orig), splist$SpCode)

#Are ALL species codes in the revised macroplot and microplot data in the list?
setdiff(unique(macro$SpCode), splist$SpCode)
setdiff(micro$SpCode, splist$SpCode)
```
The original file had 6 invalid codes: Artogoss, Ficudrpu, Ipomsp., Lantcaac, Lepideci and Neurmalb. None of them are in the species list.

**We continue using the revised data ("Macroplot_data_Rev.txt").**

#### Totals, plots and most abundant species
```{r}
# Expected: 61965 individuals, 96 plots, 400 species (incl. unidentified)
nrow(macro)
n_distinct(macro$PlotID)
n_distinct(macro$SpCode)
```
Metadata states that there are 400 spieces but we can only find 399. Looning the original file and alis checking if the unidentified category is in the macroplot data.
```{r}
#Checking if the species count was already 399 in the original metadata file
n_distinct(macro_orig$SpCode)

#Checking if the unidentified category in the macroplot data? (expected 59 individuals)
sum(macro$SpCode == "UnID")
sum(grepl("^un", macro$SpCode, ignore.case = TRUE))

#How many macroplot species does the species list explain?
length(intersect(unique(macro$SpCode), splist$SpCode))   # should equal 399

# Species-list entries that occur only in the microplots, or nowhere
micro_present <- micro$SpCode[rowSums(micro[, -1]) > 0]
length(setdiff(splist$SpCode, macro$SpCode))                   # not in macroplots
setdiff(splist$SpCode, union(macro$SpCode, micro_present))     # in neither layer
```
The revised macroplot file contains 61,965 individuals in 96 plots and 399 taxa (398 named taxa + the unidentified category, UnID, 59 individuals). The metadata states 400 taxa, but the original file also contains 399, so the difference is an error in the metadata, not in the data. The revision only corrected six misspelled species codes one for one (e.g. Ficudrpu → Ficudrup); no taxa were merged. All 446 entries of the species list occur in the data: 399 in the macroplots and 47 only in the microplots.

```{r}
#Do plot codes match the site table (both directions)?
setdiff(unique(macro$PlotID), sites$PlotID)
setdiff(sites$PlotID, unique(macro$PlotID))
```
we can see that every plot in the macroplot data exists in the site table.
The second shows that Site_variables.txt has a row whose PlotID is an empty string "". Let’s look at that row before deciding what to do with it:

```{r}
#How many rows does the site table have? (expected 96)
nrow(sites)

#Which row(s) have an empty PlotID, and what do they contain?
which(sites$PlotID == "" | is.na(sites$PlotID))
sites[sites$PlotID == "" | is.na(sites$PlotID), ]

sum(sites$PlotID != "")  #are there 96 real (non-empty) plot codes
anyDuplicated(sites$PlotID[sites$PlotID != ""]) #are plot id-s unique
```
The site table has 98 rows. Rows 97 and 98 have no PlotID
```{r}
# Rows 97-98 of Site_variables.txt have no PlotID
empty_rows <- sites$PlotID == "" | is.na(sites$PlotID)
stopifnot(all(is.na(sites[empty_rows, ]) | sites[empty_rows, ] == ""))
sites <- sites[!empty_rows, ] #removing empty rows

nrow(sites)                                     # 96
setdiff(sites$PlotID, unique(macro$PlotID))     # character(0)
```
```{r}
# Expected: Termpani = 3811, Xylixylo = 3498, Oleadioi = 2311
macro_sp_tot <- macro %>% count(SpCode, name = "n_ind", sort = TRUE)
head(macro_sp_tot, 5)

# Expected: 33 species with total abundance of 1
sum(macro_sp_tot$n_ind == 1)

# Unidentified individuals; metadata uses both "UnID" and "UniID" -> check both
# Expected: 59 unidentified individuals
macro_sp_tot %>% filter(grepl("^Un", SpCode))
grep("^Un", splist$SpCode, value = TRUE)
```
```{r}
# Is Oleadioi also 2366 in the original file?
sum(macro_orig$SpCode == "Oleadioi")

# Does any species have exactly 2311 individuals? (typo in the metadata?)
macro_sp_tot %>% filter(n_ind == 2311)

# In how many plots does Oleadioi occur?
macro %>% filter(SpCode == "Oleadioi") %>% count(PlotID, sort = TRUE) %>% nrow()
```
The total of 61,965 individuals, the counts of the two most abundant species (Termpani 3811, Xylixylo 3498), the 33 singleton species and the 59 unidentified individuals all match the metadata. Olea dioica (Oleadioi) has 2366 individuals in both the original and the revised file, while the metadata reports 2311. No species has 2311 individuals. The difference (55) equals the number of plots in which O. dioica occurs, which suggests a counting error in the metadata rather than in the data. 

The unidentified category is coded UnID in the data and in the species list, but UniID in the metadata’s variable definitions.

#### Girth values
The value 0 in TreeGirth2–TreeGirth5 means the stem does not exist.
TreeGirth1 must be ≥ 10 cm, and extra stems are listed in decreasing order.
```{r}
girth_cols <- paste0("TreeGirth", 1:5)

#Missing values per girth column (should be none)
colSums(is.na(macro[girth_cols]))
#No missing values
```
```{r}
#Main stem below the 10 cm threshold (should be 0)
sum(macro$TreeGirth1 < 10, na.rm = TRUE)
#yes, it is 0
```
```{r}
#Extra stems between 0 and 10 cm (should be 0)
sapply(macro[girth_cols[-1]], function(x) sum(x > 0 & x < 10, na.rm = TRUE))
#yes, it is 0
```
```{r}
#Stems out of decreasing order (should be 0)
sapply(2:5, function(i) {
  sum(macro[[girth_cols[i]]] > macro[[girth_cols[i - 1]]], na.rm = TRUE)
  #yes, it is 0
})
```
```{r}
#A stem recorded after a missing one, e.g. Girth3 > 0 while Girth2 = 0 (should be 0)
sapply(3:5, function(i) {
  sum(macro[[girth_cols[i]]] > 0 & macro[[girth_cols[i - 1]]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
})
#yes, it is 0
```
```{r}
#Plausibility of the largest trees (girth in cm)
summary(macro$TreeGirth1) #summary table with column min and max
macro %>% arrange(desc(TreeGirth1)) %>% head(5) #looking at the max top5 values
```
All girth values follow the rules in the metadata: no missing values, all main stems ≥ 10 cm gbh, extra stems either 0 (no stem) or ≥ 10 cm and listed in decreasing order. 
Girth ranges from 10 to 1048 cm (median 28 cm). 
The largest trees, a Ficus virens with 3.3 m diameter (BSP36) and three Dysoxylum malabaricum of 2.4–2.7 m diameter (BSP104), are plausible for strangler figs and old-growth wet evergreen forest, so no girth values were changed.

### 2.2 Microplot data
```{r}
glimpse(micro)
```
Dimensions match the metadata: 334 species (rows) and 97 columns (SpCode + 96 plots).

```{r}
setdiff(micro$SpCode, splist$SpCode)
```
Microplot data uses Lepideci and Neurmalb, but those are not in the species list.

```{r}
code_fix <- sp_changes %>% distinct(SpCode_orig, SpCode_rev)

# Does the corrected name already exist in micro? (then the rows must be merged)
micro %>% filter(SpCode %in% c(code_fix$SpCode_orig, code_fix$SpCode_rev)) %>%
  select(SpCode)

micro <- micro %>%
  left_join(code_fix, by = c("SpCode" = "SpCode_orig")) %>%
  mutate(SpCode = coalesce(SpCode_rev, SpCode)) %>%
  select(-SpCode_rev) %>%
  group_by(SpCode) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Checks after correction
setdiff(micro$SpCode, splist$SpCode)   # should be character(0)
dim(micro)                             # 334 x 97 if no rows were merged
sum(micro[, -1])                       # still 14848
```

The 2011 revision corrected six misspelled species codes only in the macroplot file. Two of them (Lepideci, Neurmalb) also occur in the microplot file, which was not revised. They were corrected in code using the same mapping as in the revised macroplot file (Lepideci → Lepidefi, Neurmalb → Neurmala).

Looking if the site columns match the PlotIDs of the site table (both directions)?
```{r}
micro_sites <- setdiff(names(micro), "SpCode")
setdiff(micro_sites, sites$PlotID)
setdiff(sites$PlotID, micro_sites)
```
Both lists are empty, so the 96 site columns in the microplot file match the 96 PlotIDs in the site table.

```{r}
# Duplicated species rows
micro$SpCode[duplicated(micro$SpCode)]
```
List is empty so there are no duplicated species rows.
```{r}
# Abundances must be non-negative whole numbers without NA
micro_mat <- as.matrix(micro[, micro_sites])
sum(is.na(micro_mat))
range(micro_mat, na.rm = TRUE)
all(micro_mat == round(micro_mat), na.rm = TRUE)
```
The values are clean and there are no missing values. All are whole numbers, which are ranging from 0 to 224.
```{r}
# Expected: 14848 individuals in total
sum(micro_mat)

# Expected: Psynigr = 749, Aporlind = 624, Dichgelo = 609
micro_sp_tot <- data.frame(SpCode = micro$SpCode, n_ind = rowSums(micro_mat)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_ind))
head(micro_sp_tot, 5)
```

```{r}
# Expected: 50 species with total abundance of 1
sum(micro_sp_tot$n_ind == 1)

# Species never recorded and plots with no regeneration
sum(micro_sp_tot$n_ind == 0)
colnames(micro_mat)[colSums(micro_mat) == 0]
```
### 2.3 Site data
```{r}
glimpse(sites)
```

```{r}
# Expected: 96 unique plots
nrow(sites)
sites$PlotID[duplicated(sites$PlotID)]

# Missing values per column (FlorIntegr is NA by design for deciduous types)
colSums(is.na(sites))

# Column sums given in the metadata vs. observed
expected_sums <- c(LatDec = 1374.67111, LongDec = 7192.58583, Alt = 51683,
                   CanoHt = 1786, CanoCov = 4335, Strata = 241, Rain = 301926,
                   DryMo = 557, StrucIntegr = 181, FlorIntegr = 111)
observed_sums <- sapply(names(expected_sums),
                        function(v) sum(sites[[v]], na.rm = TRUE))
data.frame(expected = expected_sums,
           observed = round(observed_sums, 5),
           difference = round(observed_sums - expected_sums, 5))
```

```{r}
# Value ranges of the numeric variables
summary(sites[, c("LatDec", "LongDec", "Alt", "CanoHt", "CanoCov",
                  "Strata", "Rain", "DryMo")])

# Coordinates outside the study area given in the metadata
# (74°15'–75°40' E = 74.25–75.667; 13°30'–15°15' N = 13.5–15.25)
sites %>%
  filter(!between(LongDec, 74.25, 75.667) | !between(LatDec, 13.5, 15.25)) %>%
  select(PlotID, ForestDiv, LatDec, LongDec)

# Canopy cover must be 0–100 %
sites %>% filter(CanoCov < 0 | CanoCov > 100) %>% select(PlotID, CanoCov)
```

```{r}
# Categorical codes must match the codes defined in the metadata
forest_codes <- c("ATT", "DDD", "DDD+P", "DHP", "DP", "KAN",
                  "LTD", "MSA", "PDH", "PPH")
soil_codes   <- c("S2", "S3", "S4", "S6", "S7", "S8", "S10", "S11", "S13")

setdiff(unique(sites$ForestType), forest_codes)
setdiff(unique(sites$Soil), soil_codes)
setdiff(unique(sites$StrucIntegr), 1:3)
setdiff(unique(na.omit(sites$FlorIntegr)), 1:3)

table(sites$ForestType, useNA = "ifany")
table(sites$Soil, useNA = "ifany")
table(sites$ForestDiv, useNA = "ifany")

# FlorIntegr should be NA exactly for the deciduous types ATT and LTD
table(ForestType = sites$ForestType, FlorIntegr_NA = is.na(sites$FlorIntegr))
```
The site table contains 96 unique plots with valid codes for forest type, soil and integrity classes. The only missing values are in FlorIntegr (28 plots), which are exactly the deciduous types ATT (8) and LTD (20), for which floristic integrity is not defined. Value ranges are plausible (rainfall 776–8340 mm/yr, dry season 4–7 months, altitude 55–1060 m, canopy cover 0–80 %). 
Some plots lie slightly outside the coordinate range given in the metadata (minimum 13.23° N and 74.15° E, maximum 75.82° E), but within the study districts. 
The design is unbalanced: forest types range from 24 plots (PDH) to a single plot (DP), so rare types must be merged or excluded in group comparisons. 
Dry-season length varies little (most plots 6 months), and several plots share identical interpolated rainfall values, which shows that some plots are spatially clustered.

### 2.4 Spiecies data
```{r}
glimpse(splist)
```

```{r}
# Expected: 446 species (incl. unidentified category), codes unique
nrow(splist)
splist$SpCode[duplicated(splist$SpCode)] #no duplicates
splist$Name[duplicated(splist$Name) & !is.na(splist$Name)] #no duplicates
```
```{r}
# Is any old name (Synonym) also listed as a current species name?
intersect(splist$Synonym, splist$Name)
```
```{r}
table(splist$Habit, useNA = "ifany")
table(splist$Pheno, useNA = "ifany")
table(splist$WGEnd, useNA = "ifany")
```
Each trait column has exactly one NA. It should unidentified category UnID, which has no species information, as the metadata says. Confirming it in code:

```{r}
splist %>% filter(is.na(Habit) | is.na(Pheno) | is.na(WGEnd)) %>%   #filter those column where row in NA
  select(SpCode, Name, Habit, Pheno, WGEnd)                         #show thise columns
```

```{r}
#According to the metadata, a species code is the first 4 letters of the genus plus the first 4 letters of the species epithet
#Looking at the codes that dont match the metadata description
splist %>% 
  filter(nchar(SpCode) != 8) %>%      #count the characters in each code and keep only codes that are not 8 characters long
  select(SpCode, Name, Family, Habit) #show only these four columns,
```

We can see misspelled species name in the species list. Strynux has the name “Strychnos nuxNAvomica”. The real name is Strychnos nux-vomica. NA is where the hyphen should be.
```{r}
# The species name of Strynux contains "NA" instead of a "-"
splist %>% filter(SpCode == "Strynux") %>% 
  select(SpCode, Name)

splist <- splist %>%
  mutate(Name = sub("nuxNAvomica", "nux-vomica", Name, fixed = TRUE))

splist %>% filter(SpCode == "Strynux") %>% select(SpCode, Name)   # Strychnos nux-vomica
```

### 2.5 Consistency between files
```{r}
# Species in the list that occur in neither layer (should be none)
setdiff(splist$SpCode, union(macro$SpCode, micro$SpCode))

# Number of species per layer and in total (uses the corrected micro table)
micro_present <- micro$SpCode[rowSums(micro[, -1]) > 0]

length(unique(macro$SpCode))                 # 399 macroplot taxa
length(micro_present)                        # 334 microplot taxa
length(setdiff(micro_present, macro$SpCode)) # 47 found only in microplots
length(union(macro$SpCode, micro_present))   # 446 = species list
```
The floristic integrity class (FlorIntegr) is defined in the metadata from the share of individuals that belong to deciduous species: 1 = less than 33 %, 2 = 33–66 %, 3 = more than 66 %. 
We recalculate it from the macroplot data to see whether the published classes are reproducible.
```{r}
flor_check <- macro %>%
  left_join(splist %>% select(SpCode, Pheno), by = "SpCode") %>%
  group_by(PlotID) %>%
  summarise(pct_decid = 100 * mean(Pheno == "D", na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(FlorIntegr_calc = cut(pct_decid, breaks = c(-Inf, 33, 66, Inf),
                               labels = FALSE)) %>%
  left_join(sites %>% select(PlotID, ForestType, FlorIntegr), by = "PlotID")

table(published = flor_check$FlorIntegr,
      calculated = flor_check$FlorIntegr_calc, useNA = "ifany")

# Plots where the published and recalculated class differ
flor_check %>%
  filter(!is.na(FlorIntegr), FlorIntegr != FlorIntegr_calc) %>%
  arrange(PlotID) #nothing differs - empty tibble
```
All species in the species list occur in at least one layer: 399 taxa in the macroplots and 47 only in the microplots (446 in total, after correcting the two misspelled microplot codes). The floristic integrity classes could be reproduced exactly from the share of deciduous individuals in the macroplot data: all 68 potentially evergreen plots received the published class, and all 28 deciduous plots (ATT, LTD) contained more than 66 % deciduous individuals, as stated in the metadata.


**Conculusion**

The data are internally consistent and of good quality. Totals, column sums and trait counts match the metadata, all girth values follow the measurement rules. We found three errors in the data files, which must be corrected in code before analysis, and several inconsistencies in the metadata text, which do not affect the data.

| Problem | File | Correction |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Six misspelled species codes (e.g. Ficudrpu, Artogoss; 91 trees) | Macroplot_data.txt | Use the revised file Macroplot_data_Rev.txt |
| 2. Two of these codes (Lepideci, Neurmalb) remain in the microplot file, which was never revised | Microplot_data.txt | Recode to Lepidefi and Neurmala using the same mapping as the revision |
| 3. Two empty rows (97–98) at the end of the file | Site_variables.txt | Remove rows without PlotID |
| 4. Species name "Strychnos nuxNAvomica" | Species_list.txt | Correct to "Strychnos nux-vomica" |


**Inconsistencies in the metadata (documented, no change to the data):**

- The macroplots contain 399 taxa (398 + unidentified), not 400 as stated in the metadata.
- *Olea dioica* (Oleadioi) has 2366 individuals, not 2311. The difference (55) equals the number of plots where it occurs.
- Several codes are spelled differently in the metadata than in the data: Psynigr (data: Psycnigr), Strobsp1 (Strosp1), Syzisp. (Syzysp.), Calasp (Calasp.) and UniID (UnID).
- Microplots are described as "0.1 ha" but measure 10 × 10 m = 0.01 ha, so the pooled regeneration sample per plot covers 300 m².
- Ten plots lie outside the coordinate range given in the metadata, though within the study districts.


## 3. Clean data tables
### 3.1 Site table

```{r}
env <- sites %>%
  # numeric plot order: BSP1, BSP2, ... instead of BSP1, BSP10, BSP100
  arrange(as.numeric(sub("BSP", "", PlotID))) %>%
  mutate(
    # forest types ordered from the driest to the wettest (median rainfall)
    ForestType  = reorder(factor(ForestType), Rain, FUN = median),
    # three groups with enough plots for group comparisons
    ForestGroup = factor(case_when(ForestType == "ATT" ~ "Dry deciduous",
                                   ForestType == "LTD" ~ "Moist deciduous",
                                   TRUE                ~ "Evergreen"),
                         levels = c("Dry deciduous", "Moist deciduous", "Evergreen")),
    # disturbance as labelled factor; StrucIntegr stays numeric (1-3)
    Disturbance = factor(StrucIntegr, levels = 1:3,
                         labels = c("Slightly", "Moderately", "Highly")),
    Soil        = factor(Soil, levels = soil_codes),
    ForestDiv   = factor(ForestDiv),
    FlorIntegr  = factor(FlorIntegr, levels = 1:3)   # NA for ATT and LTD by design
  )
rownames(env) <- env$PlotID

# Checks
str(env)
head(env$PlotID)                          # BSP1, BSP2, BSP3, ...
levels(env$ForestType)                    # dry -> wet
table(env$ForestGroup)
table(env$ForestType, env$Disturbance)    # plots per forest type and disturbance
```
### 3.2 Macroplot community table

The unidentified individuals (UnID, 59 lianas) are removed, because they are not one taxon and would act as an artificial species. Genus-level taxa and morphospecies are kept as single taxa.

```{r}
#plots x species abundance table of trees >= 10 cm gbh
macro_clean <- macro %>% filter(SpCode != "UnID")

#table() counts trees per plot and species; plots in the same order as env
comm_macro <- as.data.frame.matrix(
  table(factor(macro_clean$PlotID, levels = env$PlotID), macro_clean$SpCode)
)
#Checks
dim(comm_macro)                                 #96 plots x 398 taxa
sum(comm_macro)                                 #61906 = 61965 - 59 UnID
identical(rownames(comm_macro), env$PlotID)     #TRUE: same plot order as env

comm_macro[1:5, 1:6]                            #look part of the table
```
### 3.3 Microplot community table

The microplot file is stored as species x plots. It is transposed to plots x species, with plots in the same order as the site table. 
Species codes were already corrected in section 2.2.

```{r}
#plots x species abundance table of the regeneration layer (gbh < 10 cm, height > 1 m, three 10 x 10 m microplots pooled per plot)

micro_clean <- micro %>% filter(SpCode != "UnID")   #same rule as macroplots

# select plot columns in env order, transpose, use species codes as column names
comm_micro <- as.data.frame(t(as.matrix(micro_clean[, env$PlotID]))) #plot columns in the order of the site table.
colnames(comm_micro) <- micro_clean$SpCode

# Checks
dim(comm_micro)                                 #96 plots x 334 taxa
sum(comm_micro)                                 #14848
identical(rownames(comm_micro), env$PlotID)     #TRUE: same plot order as env

comm_micro[1:5, 1:6]                            #look part of the table
```
### 3.4 Save the clean data

```{r}
# All tables must have the same plots in the same order (stops with an error if not)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(comm_macro), env$PlotID),
          identical(rownames(comm_micro), env$PlotID))

dir.create("Data/clean", showWarnings = FALSE)
save(env, macro_clean, comm_macro, comm_micro, splist,
     file = "Data/clean/clean_data.RData")
```

**Clean data for the group** — load with `load("Data/clean/clean_data.RData")`:

| Object | Content | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `env` | Site table: coordinates, climate, forest type (dry → wet), ForestGroup, Disturbance, soil | 96 plots |
| `macro_clean` | Tree list with girths (0 = no stem), UnID removed | 61,906 trees |
| `comm_macro` | Trees ≥ 10 cm gbh, individuals per plot × species | 96 × 398 |
| `comm_micro` | Regeneration (< 10 cm gbh, > 1 m), individuals per plot × species | 96 × 334 |
| `splist` | Species traits: name, family, habit, phenology, endemism | 446 taxa |

```{r}

```
